sessionTitle: Real-Time Intelligence: Building event-driven AI apps and agents

announcements.name: Custom Stream Connector (private preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Developers can build their own connector, upload the package, and have Fabric host it to bring custom sources into an Eventstream.
announcements.longDescription: The Custom Stream Connector, currently in private preview, lets developers build their own connector, upload the package, and have Fabric host that connector to bring data from their own sources into an Eventstream. It addresses the need for developers who don't want to be limited to the connectors provided out of the box and have their own data sources. It complements the broader Eventstream capabilities such as SQL semantics, multiple destinations, and developer productivity features.

announcements.name: New and expanded Eventstream connectors
announcements.shortDescription: Includes a new MQTT version, an Oracle DB Change Data connector, HTTP/REST endpoint ingestion, and a MirrorDB Change Feed connector, with roughly 40 connectors total.
announcements.longDescription: Eventstream's connector catalog spans dozens of connectors and keeps growing, with several newly launched options highlighted. These include a new MQTT version, an Oracle DB Change Data Connector, an HTTP connector for pulling data automatically from REST endpoints, and a MirrorDB Change Feed Connector for getting change data feeds from databases, Delta Tables, and mirror databases. Additional connectors are on deck and will be available soon.

announcements.name: DeltaFlow (public preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Simplifies processing Debezium CDC events, adapting to source schema changes, and managing hundreds or thousands of source tables into Eventhouse.
announcements.longDescription: DeltaFlow is a public preview feature that quickly converts CDC events into an analytics-ready form and sends them to an Eventhouse. In the demo, SQL CDC from Azure SQL is used as an Eventstream source, with DeltaFlow handling schema registry storage and creating separate tables in Eventhouse for each source table. It abstracts away details like CDC resume handling, performing the initial snapshot replication so SQL database changes become available in the Eventhouse within seconds.

announcements.name: Delta Change Feed connector (public preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Works with mirror databases and, soon, general lakehouse Delta Tables.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft is introducing the public preview of a Delta Change Feed connector for Eventstreams, since a lot of data now lives in Delta Tables in Fabric as part of a mirror database rather than only in relational databases. It works with mirror databases today and will soon work with general lakehouse Delta Tables. It was presented alongside related capabilities such as DeltaFlow, Spark Structured Streaming, Fabric Business Events, and Eventstream Observability.

announcements.name: Eventhouse MCP and Fabric Skills
announcements.shortDescription: Every Eventhouse endpoint exposes a remote MCP URL so agents can query live data, define rules in natural language, and use reusable skills via tools like GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code.
announcements.longDescription: With Real-Time Intelligence, Eventhouse MCP lets agents directly ask questions over live data and get instant insights, and MCP is also enabled for other items like Activator where rules and alerts can be defined in natural language. Fabric Skills give agents reusable capabilities and domain knowledge for interacting with Real-Time Intelligence items, connecting to tools like GitHub CLI and Claude Code. In the demo, Fabric Skills are installed and listed within GitHub Copilot CLI, including Eventhouse, Eventstream Authoring, and Consumption Skills, enabling agents to reason, act, and detect in real time.

announcements.name: Operations Agent (generally available)
announcements.shortDescription: An autonomous virtual team member that observes, analyzes, decides, and acts 24/7, publishing into Microsoft Teams with recommended actions and root-cause analysis.
announcements.longDescription: The Operations Agent is now generally available, taking the observe, analyze, decide, and act stages and running that loop autonomously. It acts like a new virtual team member on the operations team that can reason, understand, and act to help the organization move at the speed of the business. It was presented as the point where the broader Real-Time Intelligence capabilities, including the Anomaly Detector, come together.

announcements.name: Anomaly Detector (public preview)
announcements.shortDescription: Lets non-data-scientists select an out-of-box model fitted to their data's seasonality and emit anomaly events for the organization to subscribe to.
announcements.longDescription: Anomaly Detector is a public preview capability that makes it easy to leverage streaming data stored in Eventhouse and configure the right anomaly detection model for specific data with just a couple of clicks. It is designed so users don't have to be data scientists, analyzing the provided data to determine which out-of-box models best fit its seasonality and patterns. Detected anomaly events can then be published and emitted for the rest of the organization to subscribe to.
